D 71, 195, Sec. 4.2); the statement that the model has low sensitivity above 2 x 10^8 s^-1 is from the Chhetri thesis (TU Darmstadt 2018, chapter 4, p. 54). conflicts: 1S0 - 1P1 centre in 254No: gas cell 29 961.457 (+0.041/-0.007) cm^-1 (Nature 2016, 95 mbar argon, not pressure-shift corrected) versus gas jet 29 961.480(2)(12) cm^-1 (Phys. Rev. Research 2024, before Doppler correction). After the 1725(150) MHz Doppler correction the authors state a 2400 MHz (0.08 cm^-1, 1.6 sigma) discrepancy and leave it open. The gas-cell value is kept as the entry because all isotope shifts and the ionization potential are referred to it.

The 2024 gas-jet paper prints its centroid twice: '29 951.480(2)(10)' in Sec. IV B and '29 961.480(2)(12)' in Sec. IV C; the first is a misprint (the stated +700 MHz offset from 29 961.457 fits only the second).
Hyperfine B of 253No 7s7p 1P1: 2.82(69) GHz in Table I of Raeder et al. 2018 (and in the thesis table), 2.82(67) GHz in the text of the same paper (and the thesis text); 690 MHz is stored.

Lifetime of 7s7p 1P1: (2 +- 1) ns deduced from the saturation fit (same information as A = 4.2e8 s^-1), versus apparent decay times of the delayed signal of 8.5(2.2) ns (thesis) / 'about 5 ns' (Phys. Rev. Lett.), which are lengthened by the 18 ns laser pulses and jitter. No direct radiative-lifetime measurement exists; none of the three is stored as 'lifetime'.

3D3 level: 29 652 (+8/-1) cm^-1 in Phys. Rev. Lett. 120, 263003, 29 651.5 (+8/-1) cm^-1 in the thesis; convergence limit 23 792 versus 23 792.21 cm^-1. The first Rydberg analysis (Nature 2016, seven levels, limit 23 785 (+11/-1) cm^-1) could not tell which level the series started from and is superseded.

Calculated ionization potential by the configuration-interaction + all-order method is quoted as 54 390 +- 1100 cm^-1 in Table I of Phys. Rev. Lett. 120, 263003 and as 53 738 +- 500 cm^-1 in Table 5.1 of the thesis (theory, not stored).
Half-life of 252No: 2.46 s in the IAEA table, 2.4 s / 2.42(6) s in the laser papers.

Filament temperature for 254No release: about 1350 K in Nature 2016 and Phys. Rev. Lett. 120, 263003, 1050 degrees C (about 1320 K) in Phys. Rev. Lett. 120, 232503 and Eur. Phys. J. D 71, 195 (no effect on the data).
not_found: energies of the individual Rydberg levels of 254No (29 levels): shown only in figures of Phys. Rev. Lett. 120, 263003, Nature 538, 495 and the Chhetri thesis; no table printed in any source opened (Supplemental Material of the letter not located)

direct (decay-curve) measurement of the radiative lifetime of 7s7p 1P1: none exists in the sources opened; only the saturation-deduced Einstein coefficient and delayed-ionization decay times blurred by the 18 ns laser pulses
radiative lifetime, hyperfine structure and J of the level at 29 652 cm^-1: not measured (term 3D3 is an assignment)
any measured level other than 7s7p 1P1, the level at 29 652 cm^-1 and the Rydberg series: none; 7s7p 3P0,1,2, 7s6d 3D1,2, 1D2 and 7s8s are known only from calculations (entered with method 'theory')
ground-state or 1P1 g-factors, branching ratios, oscillator strengths of other lines, 1S0 - 3P1 intercombination line: no measurement
pressure shift of the 1S0 - 1P1 line in argon for nobelium itself: not measured (estimated from thallium / ytterbium; the 2024 paper announces a measurement)
isotope shifts or hyperfine structure of isotopes other than 252, 253, 254, 255No (including the K isomer of 254No): none published in the sources opened
Chhetri et al., Acta Phys. Polon. B 49, 599 (2018) (pressure shift of ytterbium Rydberg levels) was not opened; its result is quoted from the letter and the thesis

Borschevsky et al., Phys. Rev. A 75, 042514 (2007), Liu et al., Phys. Rev. A 76, 062503 (2007) and Indelicato et al., Eur. Phys. J. D 45, 155 (2007) (the calculated transition rates 5.0, 3.5 and 2.7 x 10^8 s^-1) were not opened
notes: Nobelium exists only as single atoms from heavy-ion fusion (a few 254No ions per second at GSI Darmstadt); everything measured comes from two-step resonance ionization with detection by alpha decay. MEASURED: (1) the line 5f14 7s2 1S0 - 5f14 7s7p 1P1 at 29 961.457 cm^-1 in 254No with its Einstein coefficient (deduced from the saturation curve by a rate-equation fit, not from a decay curve), (2) its isotope shifts for 252, 253, 255No relative to 254No and the hyperfine constants of 253No, (3) the ionization potential 53 444.0(4) cm^-1 from a Rydberg series, (4) one further level at 29 652 (+8/-1) cm^-1, reached only by buffer-gas collisions from 1P1 and located through the convergence limit of two Rydberg series; its label 3D3 is an assignment. All wavenumbers were measured in 65-95 mbar argon and are not corrected for the pressure shift except the ionization potential. CALCULATED (method 'theory', energies only, accuracy a few hundred cm^-1): the eight other low levels in levels_not_in_nist from Dzuba, Safronova & Safronova 2014; their calculated g-factors are under 'g_J_theory' so that they cannot be mistaken for measurements. Isotope shifts are nu(first) - nu(second) in MHz: lighter isotopes lie at higher frequency (field shift dominates). frequency_THz values are derived from printed wavenumbers. Asymmetric uncertainties are stored as unc_plus / unc_minus with 'unc' = the larger side. Nuclear moments of 253No are not purely experimental: they combine the measured A and B with calculated atomic factors (B_e/J = -6.3(0.9) GHz I/mu_N, electric field gradient 0.476(70) GHz/eb, field-shift constant -95.8(7.0) GHz/fm^2). Non-schema keys used: unc_plus, unc_minus, wavenumber_cm, half_life, mu_*, Q_*, g_J_theory, collisional_decay_time, lifetime_not_direct, buffer_gas_quenching, rydberg_series, value_range_cm, saturation_photon_flux_note, alternatives, isotope.
